title: You are not Guts (The Berserk Trauma)
summary: A long psychoanalysis of Guts from Berserk arguing he is a tragic hero, not an anti-hero, and that young men who idolize him copy trauma responses (isolation, rage, revenge, repressed emotion) instead of his virtues. NH ties this to the male loneliness epidemic, warns against using hatred as lifting fuel, and concludes that healing comes from relationships and becoming a more loving person.
claims: Many young men relate to Guts for the wrong reasons and copy his pathological traits instead of the virtues he tries to preserve
Guts is a tragic hero, not an anti-hero: his lone-wolf, violent traits are dysfunctional responses to his environment, not traits to emulate
The 'memefied' stoic-chad Guts seen in Instagram quotes ignores his psychological flaws, which are what make him interesting
We only learn through struggle; a character who never struggles has nothing to teach us
Using trauma, hatred or resentment (e.g. at a girl who rejected you) as lifting motivation works only for a time before that fire starts to consume you
He has used trauma as fuel himself in the past and found that the more you use it, the more of it you produce
Running from depression by being hyperproductive never fixes it; it grows until you burn out
Trauma survivors often get retraumatized because the defence mechanisms that helped them survive steer them back into traumatic situations
Turning your trauma or mental illness into your identity, as in 'trauma core', makes healing impossible
Just because a path is painful and difficult does not make it the right path; men tend to self-destruct for its own sake and must unlearn this
'Fighting your demons' is often a forward escape (fuite en avant) that avoids the root cause inside you
Revenge never heals: once achieved, you are left an empty husk, as Thorfinn finds in Vinland Saga
Without a father or friends, young men are the first generation left to figure out masculinity alone, then blamed for every failure
Men are only accepted when they bring energy and strength; show sadness and you get treated like a broken tool and cast out
Repressing emotion accumulates rage and sadness that eventually explodes, usually onto the people you love
Refusing all help out of self-sacrifice is a virtue turned pathological; keep asking for help even after being rejected
He wants to be a big brother to young men and show them how to walk the path of masculinity
Masculinity is a burden that can turn pathological if mismanaged; the answer is role models and connection, not becoming more feminine
Berserk's ultimate lesson is that relationships anchor us to our humanity; every effort to become better should aim at becoming a more loving person
Guts is a kind man in a wicked world and Griffith a wicked man in a wicked world; bad people often do well, but never let your dysfunctions become who you are
